agent_sessions.stop_reason: Diff 将 list(value) 改为 list(check(value))，其中 check 返回 iter(value)。对任意可迭代/迭代器输入，list(iter(value)) 与 list(value) 行为等价，无功能性缺陷。

findings.title: process now mutates shared state without acquiring STATE_LOCK, relying on caller-held lock
findings.trigger_condition: Any call to process(value) that occurs without the caller holding STATE_LOCK, especially when multiple threads concurrently invoke process on the same value dict.
findings.impact: Race condition on value['count'] may cause lost updates or undercounted results, leading to inconsistent shared state.
findings.explanation: The diff changes process from a pure read of value['count'] to a call to check(value), which performs a read-modify-write increment on the shared mutable state. The comment says STATE_LOCK is held by the caller, but process itself does not acquire or verify that lock. The locking contract is only a comment and not enforced; any caller that fails to acquire STATE_LOCK while holding the lock risk (or concurrent calls) will produce a data race.
findings.suggestion: Acquire STATE_LOCK inside process before calling check, or use a thread-safe atomic increment/locking structure. If the caller-held-lock pattern is intentional, document it in the function signature or docstring and add runtime assertion, e.g., assert lock.locked(), to prevent misuse.

findings.title: process() invokes check() without holding STATE_LOCK, causing a race on shared state
findings.trigger_condition: Two or more threads/coroutines call process() concurrently on the same mutable `value` mapping.
findings.explanation: The diff replaces the read-only `return value['count']` with `return check(value)`. The unchanged helper `lib.contract_30.check` mutates shared state via `value['count'] += 1` and its contract states the caller must hold STATE_LOCK. However, `process` acquires no lock before calling `check`, despite the added comment claiming STATE_LOCK is held by the caller. Concurrent invocations on the same `value` dict can interleave the read-modify-write step and lose updates.
findings.suggestion: Acquire STATE_LOCK around the call to check(value) in process (or perform the locking inside check), so the documented contract is actually satisfied and the increment is not racy.
